source_text:
Κινδυνεύει δὲ οὐχ ἁπλοῦν τι εἶναι τὸ αἴτιον τοῦ τὴν σωτηρίαν χαλεπωτέραν τοῖς πλουτοῦσι δοκεῖν ἢ τοῖς ἀχρημάτοις τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἀλλὰ ποικίλον. οἱ μὲν γὰρ αὐτόθεν καὶ προχείρως ἀκούσαντες τῆς τοῦ κυρίου φωνῆς, ὅτι ῥᾷον κάμηλος διὰ τρήματος ῥαφίδος διεκδύσεται ἢ πλούσιος εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀπογνόντες ἑαυτοὺς ὡς οὐ βιωσόμενοι, τῷ κόσμῳ πάντα χαριζόμενοι καὶ τῆς ἐνταῦθα ζωῆς ὡς μόνης ἑαυτοῖς ὑπολειπομένης ἐκκρεμασθέντες ἀπέστησαν πλέον τῆς ἐκεῖ ὁδοῦ, μηκέτι πολυπραγμονήσαντες μήτε τίνας τοὺς πλουσίους ὁ δεσπότης καὶ διδάσκαλος προσαγορεύει μήτε ὅπως τὸ ἀδύνατον ἐν ἀνθρώποις δυνατὸν γίνεται. ἄλλοι δὲ τοῦτο μὲν συνῆκαν ὀρθῶς καὶ προσηκόντως, τῶν δὲ ἔργων τῶν εἰς τὴν σωτηρίαν ἀναφερόντων ὀλιγωρήσαντες οὐ παρεσκευάσαντο τὴν δέουσαν παρασκευὴν εἰς τὸ τῶν ἐλπιζομένων τυχεῖν. λέγω δὲ ταῦτα. ἑκάτερα περὶ τῶν πλουσίων τῶν καὶ τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ σωτῆρος καὶ τῆς ἐπιφανοῦς σωτηρίας ᾐσθημένων, τῶν δὲ ἀμυήτων τῆς ἀληθείας ὀλίγον μοι μέλει.
Χρὴ τοίνυν τοὺς φιλαλήθως καὶ φιλαδέλφως . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
thought_title: Why salvation seems harder for the rich
orientation: Clement is explaining why the rich wrongly think salvation is harder for them than for those without money, and he distinguishes two mistaken responses to Jesus' saying about the camel and the needle.
pass_a_gloss: But the cause of salvation seeming harder to the rich than to those without money among men is likely not something simple, but varied. For some, having heard immediately and offhandedly the voice of the Lord, that a camel will pass through the eye of a needle more easily than a rich person into the kingdom of heaven, having despaired of themselves as not going to live, having granted everything to the world and having hung upon the life here as the only one left to themselves, departed further from the way there, no longer busying themselves either about whom the Master and Teacher calls rich or about how the impossible among men becomes possible. But others understood this correctly and fittingly, yet having neglected the works that lead to salvation, did not prepare the necessary preparation for obtaining the things hoped for. And I say these things about both groups of the rich, those who have perceived both the power of the Savior and the manifest salvation, but about the uninitiated in the truth I care little. It is necessary therefore that those who love truth and love the brethren . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

choices.why: The glossary bans 'the poor' for πτωχός; ἀχρήματος means literally 'without money,' and Clement is contrasting the rich with those who lack money, not with the spiritually poor.
ἐκεῖ means 'there,' pointing to the heavenly realm; 'the way there' preserves the spatial contrast with 'the life here' (τῆς ἐνταῦθα ζωῆς) in the same sentence.

choices.english: having despaired of themselves as not going to live
choices.why: The participle ἀπογνόντες with reflexive ἑαυτούς means 'having given up on themselves'; ὡς οὐ βιωσόμενοι gives the ground: 'as not going to live.' The future participle keeps the sense of their anticipated fate.
rejected: having despaired of themselves as not about to live
having given up on themselves as those who would not live

choices.english: having granted everything to the world
choices.why: χαρίζομαι means 'to give freely, grant, bestow as a favor'; 'granted' captures the deliberate surrender of everything to the world, while 'gave' would be too flat.
rejected: having given everything to the world
having bestowed everything on the world

choices.term: τῶν ἀμυήτων τῆς ἀληθείας ὀλίγον μοι μέλει
choices.english: about the uninitiated in the truth I care little
choices.why: ἀμύητος is a mystery-cult term for the uninitiated; Clement uses it for those outside the truth. 'Uninitiated in the truth' preserves the metaphor, and 'I care little' renders ὀλίγον μοι μέλει literally.
rejected: those not initiated into the truth

choices.english: those who love truth and love the brethren
choices.why: The adverbs φιλαλήθως and φιλαδέλφως modify an implied subject; rendering them as relative clauses 'those who love truth and love the brethren' makes the implied persons explicit in English while keeping the compound structure.
rejected: lovers of truth and of the brethren

bible_refs.note: ῥᾷον κάμηλος διὰ τρήματος ῥαφίδος διεκδύσεται ἢ πλούσιος εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν

pass_b_english: The reason salvation seems harder for the rich than for those without money is likely not a simple one, but varied. Some, hearing the Lord's voice at once and without reflection—that it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven (Mark 10:25)—despaired of themselves as having no hope of life. They granted everything to the world, hung upon the life here as the only one left to them, and turned away from the way there, no longer troubling themselves about whom the Master and Teacher calls rich, or how what is impossible for human beings becomes possible. Others understood this rightly and fittingly, but neglected the works that lead to salvation and did not make the necessary preparation to obtain what they hoped for. I say both these things about the rich who have perceived the power of the Savior and his glorious salvation; about the uninitiated in the truth I care little.
It is necessary, then, that those who love truth and love the brethren [text breaks off here]
notes: The source text ends with a lacuna after φιλαδέλφως, marked by dots in the source; the sentence is incomplete and resumes in the following section.

last_rejected.why: Greek says 'the useless of men', not 'those without money'; adds a false notion of poverty.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀχρήματος means without money/resources; 'those without money' is within normal range, not 'useless'.

problems.quote: despaired of themselves as not going to live
problems.why: Unnatural English; 'not going to live' is vague and awkward.
problems.fix: Render: 'despaired of themselves as having no hope of life.'

problems.quote: It is necessary, then, that those who love truth and love the brethren . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
problems.why: Sentence trails off into ellipses; incomplete or corrupted text with no explanation.
problems.fix: Add editorial note: '[text breaks off here]' or supply the missing portion.

edits.old: despaired of themselves as not going to live
edits.new: despaired of themselves as having no hope of life

edits.old: It is necessary, then, that those who love truth and love the brethren . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
edits.new: It is necessary, then, that those who love truth and love the brethren [text breaks off here]

fixed: The Greek ἀπογνόντες ἑαυτοὺς ὡς οὐ βιωσόμενοι means 'having despaired of themselves as not going to live'; the English 'as not going to live' is awkward and vague, so I rendered it as 'as having no hope of life' to clarify the sense.

The source text ends with a lacuna (the Greek breaks off after φιλαδέλφως), so the English ellipses are appropriate but need an editorial note; I added '[text breaks off here]' to indicate the incomplete text.
